title: The Three Summonses: How Influx Descends and Life Ascends Through Three Differently-Rooted Channels
arc: The teaching describes three "wells" or summonses — three discrete channels by which divine influx descends and the Living Soul is drawn upward — explaining how each is rooted differently between heaven and earth, why the wheel of the stars belongs to one channel but not the others, and how the threefold structure terminates in matter's self-consumption at the end.
reading:
This chapter explains a single cosmological problem: there are three distinct channels by which spiritual influx falls from the heavens onto the earth, and by which the captive Life is drawn back upward. Each channel is "rooted" differently, and on that difference the entire economy of descent and ascent depends. The Coptic word translated "well" (ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ) is essentially a summons-channel — a conduit through which the Father's call comes down and the soul's response goes up. The teaching's image is rainfall: three rains, three differently caused, three differently rooted.

The premise is laid down at the beginning. When the Father of Greatness, working through the Living Spirit, established the worlds of the upper region, he stripped the captured powers of their bodies and cast those bodies down into the lands of the lower region. The heavens above were then "rooted" in those buried corpses below; the upper worlds are psychic and pneumatic, the lower somatic. This binding-down of heavenly roots into earthly corpses is what makes a summons-channel possible at all: every heaven now has its hidden anchor in the earth, and every rising of the Life to the height passes through the corpses where it was buried. The first summons therefore comes "upon the powers of the heavens, unto their bodies and their corpses upon the earth, and back upon their bodies again": it is the foundational rain that runs between the firmaments and the buried members of the natural mind, the channel through which good is sorted out (ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄) and Error is sent back down.

The second summons is gentler and more particular. It descends from the temples, dwelling-places, and cities of the heavens down to "the five likenesses of the trees" growing upon the earth — the five-fold receptive principle in vegetative form, the natural mind in its growing capacity. The Life rises from these trees back up to the heavenly dwellings, accompanied by the array of the heavenly hosts. This is influx as quiet vegetative growth: doctrine descending into perception, perception bearing fruit, fruit drawn up through the same channel by which the call came down.

The third summons is the most troubled. Its powers are the indwellers of all the firmaments whose roots come down into "the five worlds of the flesh" — the five modes of corrupt natural life, mingled in one another. Here the influx pours down not pure but bearing desire (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ), evil (ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ), and wrath (ⲃⲗⲕⲉ); it falls upon human beings and upon the cattle (the natural affections), and at the appointed hour the heavenly powers pour out Error, scourge, and venom upon the creatures of flesh, who are then bound to one another in desire, wrath, and evil. This third channel is the mixed rain: real influx, but carrying down with it the contamination of the powers through whom it passes. It is how astrological-natural causation works upon humanity — through the energies of the eyes that are upon the height.

Then comes the disciple's question, which is the doctrinal pivot of the teaching. The student remembers that the master earlier said the Wheel has no root in this earth — yet here we hear that the stars and the zodiac-signs rule over the back of the flesh and over the Five Trees, and that everything reaching humanity (riches, poverty, sickness, health) reaches them through the zodiac and the natal star. How can both be true? The master answers that what he said before was correct and remains established in its place. When the Living Spirit established the heavens and the firmaments above, their roots were bound into the corpses cast down into the lands. But when the Wheel was established, its root was not bound into those corpses; it was bound at "the boundary of the sea." The Wheel belongs to a different rooting altogether — at the salt mingled-state of the natural, not in the buried bodies.

The reason the Wheel nevertheless reigns over flesh and trees is then given by retelling the descent of the matter. When the Third Ambassador came and revealed his image, the archons sorted out and surrendered the Light to the heavens. But the Hyle within them was cast forth toward the Ambassador's image; she rose to grasp it, failed, was shaken, and fell. In falling she spread herself into three kinds: one fell upon the Wheel, one fell to the sea, and one — through the kind that fell — into the sphere, where roots were bound into the trees and the flesh. Through this triple fall the stars and zodiac took authority over the five worlds of the flesh and the five worlds of the tree, by means of the nature that came down upon the wheel. Another root was bound in the trees through the abortions that fell, and another in the flesh; thus the stars exercise authority over trees and flesh through Sin's root and the abortions' root, both fallen downward. The Wheel itself is rootless in the deep earth, but its "branches" run through these fallen roots and so reach into flesh and tree.

Crucially, the men whom the Living Spirit bound in the lands — those whose souls rise through the elements to the heavens — are not themselves bound to the wheel. They are only "seized by the hands of the powers" that hang upon the wheel. The regenerate soul is touched by astral causation but not chained to it: its true rooting is in the corpses-channel of the first summons, not in the sea-boundary of the wheel.

The three summonses are then summarized as the three different rains the teaching set out to explain. The first comes from the firmaments down to the lands, identical with the rain that comes from the wheel down through the depth of the sea — these are one and the same channel viewed from above and below. The second is the root that runs from heaven down to the trees. The third is the one bound through the abortions in the flesh, where the fathers of the abortions in the heavens yoked their bonds to the men below by these very summonses. By these three the Father of Life draws souls upward — those mingled in the powers, bound in the lands of the entire archonic host, the place where the life of the Living Soul is drawn up out of the whole earth, its mountains, fields, and waters.

The closing movement names a hierarchy of greatness in this drawing-up. After the first great Root (the root of the trees bound to the firmaments above), there is "a great life" that will not cease coming up out of the tree and the Cross of Light in their entirety — drawn up like a great encampment, the host of redeemed truth ascending in ordered ranks. The lesser ascent goes up through the moisture of the natural, returning to the goods of the land and sustaining the whole earth in all the worlds. The teaching adds a striking geographical note: trees in the full sense exist only in the southern world, and even the flesh-bodies act fully only there; in the other regions only a small portion exists, in proportion. This locates the working theatre of redemption in one specific cosmic quarter where the channels are open in their fullness.

The teaching ends with the eschatological resolution. So long as the channels run, matter pours its mingled rain down and the soul is drawn up through three distinct rootings. But at the appointed hour, when the Light has been extracted from Hyle and her substance plundered, Matter herself will turn upon her own members and consume them. The three summonses will have completed their work; what remains of darkness, no longer fed by mingling with light, will eat itself. The whole teaching is thus a doctrine of how influx is structured in three discrete channels during the present mingled state, and why that structure is exactly the one needed to draw all the captive Life home before the final self-consumption of the unredeemed.

Several lacunae obscure details (especially in §§2926–2933 about the third summons's specific contents, and in the closing paragraphs about how the Father of Life proportions the drawing-up), but the threefold structure and its rationale are stable across the surviving text.

major_images.meaning: three discrete channels of influx and ascent: powers/corpses, trees, and flesh — three differently-rooted rains by which the Lord calls down and draws up the Living Soul

major_images.image: roots bound into corpses / into the boundary of the sea
major_images.meaning: the two distinct rootings of heaven in earth: the firmaments rooted in buried bodies (the channel of redemption), the Wheel rooted only at the salt mingled-state (astral causation that touches but does not own the regenerate soul)

major_images.image: Hyle's threefold fall after the Ambassador's revelation
major_images.meaning: the dispersal of corrupt receptivity into wheel, sea, and trees/flesh — explaining how the stars and zodiac came to exercise authority over natural life through the abortions and the root of Sin

major_images.image: the five likenesses of the trees and the five worlds of the flesh
major_images.meaning: the complete five-fold structure of receptive natural life (vegetative perception) and of corrupt natural concupiscence — the two domains the second and third summonses respectively touch

major_images.image: the great encampment of life rising from tree and Cross of Light
major_images.meaning: the ordered ascent of redeemed truth as a host drawn upward through the first great Root — the principal channel of regenerative ascent

major_images.image: Matter consuming her own members at the end
major_images.meaning: the eschatological self-consumption of unredeemed darkness once the Light has been extracted through the three summonses — the bolos-state in which falsity, no longer mingled with truth, devours itself
